title: Dakota Staton's Capitol album: tunes McRae supplied
summary: Staton recorded McRae songs including "Broadway", "You Showed Me the Way" and "Moon Ray" to finish an album in New York.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Okay. Now before we get to that, what I'd like to do is talk about some of the things you did with Dave Cavanaugh over at Capitol.
You were involved in Dakota Staton's early success with the Late Late Show.
Yeah.
She recorded Broadway and she recorded --
'You Showed Me The Way.'
'You Showed Me The Way.'
She did 'Moon Ray,' which, of course, you had a hand in.
Yeah, she did a lot of things.

MR. WELBURN: Hold on a second.
Okay, we're back to Dakota Staton. As we say, you did Broadway.
Now what hand actually did you have in this recording? You went into the studio with some of the -- with these particular tunes and you helped her put this date together -- you helped Dave Cavanaugh.
Van Alexander's name is on here. It says here, "a stirring background conceived and conducted by Van Alexander with the assist of Hank Jones," who was on piano for that date.
What actually did you do?
Hank Jones -- the band -- we put these things together like head arrangements. All what we did was that --
The tunes belonged to me, you know. When Dave had did about four things or eight -- four or five things on the coast -- he decided that since -- that he wanted to finish the album.
The album was gonna be fininished in New York. (inaudible). They were all coming here.

And Dakota Staton wanted to do two or three things that I have, you know. I say, "Well, you know, why don't you do Back Bay Shuffle."
"You Showed Me The Way" -- I give her "You Showed Me The Way," and I give her "Broadway", you know.
She say, "Well I wanna do the other thing on Artie." So I got her this song, "Moon Ray", you know.
And what we did was -- like Hank Jones and all those guys -- like great as he is today, you know, always a (inaudible) studio man. One of the greatest, you know, NBC, CBS piano player, you know.
You must remember they had all these top musicians on the date. And like we all --
At that time, we just used piano copies. See, the date was -- they call the musicians because nobody was supposed to write anything, you know.
Van probably -- I don't know what Van -- Van didn't sketch out. He probably sketched out some of the things later that we had other tunes
